paras.t: In quo Domino, id est cujus subsidio, et vos coædificamini, id est, simul cum aliis fidelibus ædificamini intus in anima, virtutibus, donis atque scientiis, in habitaculum Dei, id est, ut sitis templum inhabitationis divinæ, in Spiritu Sancto, id est virtute Spiritus Sancti, qui hujus ædificationis artifex est, et sine quo nullum acceptum est opus.
paras.en: [[2:22|In whom|In quo]], the Lord, that is, by whose aid, [[2:22|you also are built together|et vos coædificamini]], that is, you are built up together with the other faithful, inwardly in the soul, with virtues, gifts and knowledge, [[2:22|into an habitation of God|in habitaculum Dei]], that is, so that you may be a temple of the divine indwelling, [[2:22|in the Spirit|in Spiritu Sancto]], that is, by the power of the Holy Ghost, who is the builder of this building, and without whom no work is acceptable.

paras.t: Quæritur circa prædicta, quomodo ei quod dictum est, Jam non estis hospites et advenæ, consonet quod de Sanctis scriptum est alibi, Confitentes quia peregrini et hospites sunt super terram; item quod ait Petrus, Obsecro vos tanquam advenas et peregrinos; et illud denique Davidicum, Ne sileas, quoniam advena ego sum apud te et peregrinus, sicut omnes patres mei. Et respondendum, quod Sancti sunt peregrini et advenæ, quantum ad sæculum istud, in quo peregrinantur a Domino, suspirantes ad patriam supercœlestem. Mundus enim carcer est atque exilium electorum. Non autem sunt hospites, peregrini aut advenæ, quoad regnum et domum seu civitatem militantis Ecclesiæ: imo et triumphantis Ecclesiæ cives et domestici sunt in spe.
paras.en: It is asked concerning the foregoing how what was said, [[2:19|you are no more strangers and foreigners|Jam non estis hospites et advenæ]], agrees with what is written elsewhere of the saints, [[Heb 11:13|confessing that they are pilgrims and strangers on the earth|Confitentes quia peregrini et hospites sunt super terram]]; and with what Peter says, [[1 Pet 2:11|I beseech you, as strangers and pilgrims|Obsecro vos tanquam advenas et peregrinos]]; and finally with that saying of David, [[Ps 38:13|Be no silent: for I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner as all my fathers were|Ne sileas, quoniam advena ego sum apud te et peregrinus, sicut omnes patres mei]]. And the answer must be that the saints are pilgrims and strangers as regards this world, in which they are pilgrims away from the Lord, sighing for the fatherland above the heavens; for the world is the prison and exile of the elect. But they are not strangers, pilgrims or foreigners as regards the kingdom and the house or city of the Church militant: nay, they are even citizens and domestics of the Church triumphant, in hope.

3.title: EXPLICATIO CAPITULI TERTII : HUJUS REI GRATIA, EGO PAULUS VINCTUS, ETC.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: For this cause, I Paul, the prisoner, etc.

paras.t: Orans præterea sanctus Apostolus pro Ephesiis, ait : Hujus rei gratia, id est pro hac causa mihi grata, et vobis gratiosa, videlicet ut ædificemini in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu Sancto (secundum intellectum jam expressum), ego Paulus vinctus Jesu Christi, id est propter Christum Romæ incarceratus et vinculis strictus, pro vobis gentibus, id est ob hoc quod vobis gentibus evangelizo. Et hoc vobis constare potest sic esse, si tamen audistis dispensationem gratiæ Dei quæ data est mihi, id est gratiam mihi ex divina dispensatione seu dispositione collatam, videlicet apostolatum et cetera dona gratis data atque gratifica mihi impensa, in vobis, id est ad vestram salutem et instructionem. Quoniam secundum revelationem, id est ex supernaturali et clara illuminatione Christi, notum mihi factum est sacramentum, id est humanæ redemptionis mysterium seu occultum Dei consilium de salvatione hominum, sicut supra (videlicet in præcedenti capitulo) scripsi in brevi sermone, dicendo de Christo : Ipse est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum ; prout potestis, legentes verba illa, intelligere prudentiam, id est sapientiam, meam in mysterio Christi cognoscendo, id est in descriptione, prædicatione, seu cognitione hujus divini secreti, seu summæ mentis consilii, utpote quod gentes per Christum salvandæ sint.
paras.en: Praying further for the Ephesians, the holy Apostle says: [[3:1|For this cause|Hujus rei gratia]], that is, for this cause, pleasing to me and gracious to you, namely that you be built into a habitation of God in the Holy Ghost (according to the sense already set out), [[3:1|I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ|ego Paulus vinctus Jesu Christi]][[Eph 4:1||]], that is, imprisoned at Rome for Christ's sake and bound with chains, [[3:1|for you Gentiles|pro vobis gentibus]], that is, because I preach the gospel to you Gentiles. And that this is so may be plain to you, [[3:2|If yet you have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me|si tamen audistis dispensationem gratiæ Dei quæ data est mihi]], that is, the grace bestowed on me by divine dispensation or disposition, namely the apostleship and the other gifts freely given [gratis data: charisms given for others' benefit] and gracious [gratifica: sanctifying graces] granted me, [[3:2|towards you|in vobis]], that is, for your salvation and instruction. [[3:3|How that, according to revelation|Quoniam secundum revelationem]][[Gal 1:12||]], that is, by the supernatural and clear illumination of Christ, [[3:3|the mystery has been made known to me|notum mihi factum est sacramentum]], that is, the mystery of man's redemption, or the hidden counsel of God concerning the salvation of men, [[3:3|as I have written above in a few words|sicut supra scripsi in brevi]] (namely in the preceding chapter), saying of Christ: [[Eph 2:14|he is our peace, who hath made both one|Ipse est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum]]; [[3:4|As you reading|prout potestis, legentes]] those words, [[3:4|may understand my knowledge|intelligere prudentiam]], that is, my wisdom, [[3:4|in the mystery of Christ|in mysterio Christi]] in knowing it, that is, in describing, preaching or knowing this divine secret, the counsel of the supreme Mind, namely that the Gentiles were to be saved through Christ.

paras.t: Quod mysterium aliis, id est præteritis, generationibus non est agnitum, id est revelatum, scilicet filiis hominum qui fuerunt, sicut nunc, id est tam plene, tam vulgate, et tam perfecte quam modo. Revelatum autem sanctis Apostolis ejus et Prophetis novi Testamenti : quorum multi nominantur in Actibus Apostolorum. Nam et omnes Apostoli fuerunt prophetæ. His ergo revelatum est in spiritu, id est per Spiritum Sanctum ; vel, In spiritu, id est spirituali mentis excessu seu elevatione ad percipiendam revelationem divinam : esse gentes, id est electos gentiles, coheredes quoad felicitatem futuram, et concorporales, id est ad idem mysticum corpus pertinentes, et comparticipes promissionis, id est consortes cœlestium promissionum cum nobis Apostolis ceterisque electis Judæis, ita ut eadem sit beatitudo omnium nostrum in patria, et nunc unum corpus simus Christi. Quod totum factum est in Christo Jesu, id est virtute et gratia, seu per incarnationem, passionem et merita Christi ; item per Evangelium, id est evangelicæ legis prædicationem, per quam gentes ad fidem conversæ sunt, et Christi gratiam susceperunt : cujus Evangelii factus sum ego minister, id est obsequiosus annuntiator, secundum donum gratiæ Dei quæ data est mihi, id est secundum apostolatum et sapientiam mihi divinitus distributa, secundum operationem virtutis ejus, id est secundum influxum divinæ potentiæ, ad tantam me gratiam promoventis.
paras.en: [[3:5|Which|Quod]] mystery [[3:5|in other generations|aliis generationibus]], that is, past ones, [[3:5|was not known|non est agnitum]], that is, revealed, namely [[3:5|to the sons of men|filiis hominum]] who then were, [[3:5|as it is now|sicut nunc]], that is, so fully, so openly and so perfectly as now. [[3:5|revealed to his holy apostles and prophets|Revelatum autem sanctis Apostolis ejus et Prophetis]] of the New Testament, many of whom are named in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 13:1||]][[Acts 21:10||]]. For all the Apostles too were prophets. To these, then, it was revealed [[3:5|in the Spirit|in spiritu]], that is, by the Holy Ghost; or, in the spirit, that is, by a spiritual rapture or elevation of the mind to receive the divine revelation: [[3:6|That the Gentiles|esse gentes]], that is, the elect Gentiles, [[3:6|should be fellow heirs|coheredes]] as to the happiness to come, [[3:6|and of the same body|et concorporales]], that is, belonging to the same mystical body, [[3:6|and copartners of his promise|et comparticipes promissionis]], that is, sharers in the heavenly promises with us Apostles and the other elect Jews, so that the beatitude of us all in the fatherland is the same, and we are now one body of Christ. All this was done [[3:6|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, by the power and grace, or through the incarnation, passion and merits of Christ; and [[3:6|by the gospel|per Evangelium]], that is, by the preaching of the gospel law, through which the Gentiles were converted to the faith and received the grace of Christ: [[3:7|Of which I am made a minister|cujus Evangelii factus sum ego minister]], that is, a dutiful herald of the Gospel, [[3:7|according to the gift of the grace of God, which is given to me|secundum donum gratiæ Dei quæ data est mihi]], that is, according to the apostleship and wisdom divinely dealt out to me, [[3:7|according to the operation of his power|secundum operationem virtutis ejus]], that is, according to the inflowing of the divine might which raised me to so great a grace.

paras.t: Mihi enim Paulo omnium sanctorum minimo, non simpliciter, sed secundum aliquam considerationem, videlicet quantum ad id quod sum ex me ipso, et quod feci adversus Ecclesiam. Etenim secundum diversas considerationes sui ipsius, potest homo diverso de sese judicare modo sine mendacio, sicque major ac perfectior potest se vere humiliare sub inferioribus. Nunquam enim debet aliquis propter humilitatem a veritate recedere. Data est gratia hæc, id est auctoritas et sapientia : in gentibus evangelizare, id est gentibus prædicare, investigabiles divitias, id est imperscrutabilia et copiosissima dona et beneficia Christi hominibus præstita vel promissa : et illuminare instrumentaliter, id est prædicando docere, omnes gentes, id est quasdam de omni genere gentium, quæ sit dispensatio, id est executio seu dispensativa adimpletio, sacramenti absconditi a sæculis in Deo, id est humanæ redemptionis secreto consilio factæ, seu incarnationis Filii Dei. Quod sacramentum, absconditum seu celatum fuit in Deo, id est in divinæ mentis notitia, a sæculis, id est ab omnium generationum exordiis, utpote ab origine mundi, ita ut nulli creaturæ angelicæ vel humanæ fuerit plene manifestatum. Qui Deus omnia creavit. Ut innotescat principibus et potestatibus in cœlestibus per Ecclesiam multiformis sapientia Dei, secundum præfinitionem sæculorum, quam fecit Deus in Christo Jesu Domino nostro.
paras.en: For [[3:8|To me, the least of all the saints|Mihi enim Paulo omnium sanctorum minimo]], Paul[[1 Cor 15:9||]]: not simply, but under a certain consideration, namely as to what I am of myself, and what I did against the Church. For according to different considerations of himself a man can judge of himself in different ways without lying, and so one who is greater and more perfect can truly humble himself beneath his inferiors. For no one ought ever to depart from the truth for the sake of humility. [[3:8|is given this grace|Data est gratia hæc]], that is, authority and wisdom: [[3:8|to preach among the Gentiles|in gentibus evangelizare]], that is, to preach to the Gentiles, [[3:8|the unsearchable riches|investigabiles divitias]], that is, the inscrutable and most abundant gifts and benefits [[3:8|of Christ|Christi]] bestowed or promised to men: [[3:9|And to enlighten|et illuminare]] instrumentally, that is, to teach by preaching, [[3:9|all men|omnes]] nations, that is, some of every kind of nation, [[3:9|what is the dispensation|quæ sit dispensatio]], that is, the carrying out or dispensing fulfilment, [[3:9|of the mystery which hath been hidden from eternity in God|sacramenti absconditi a seculis in Deo]], that is, of man's redemption, wrought by a secret counsel, or of the incarnation of the Son of God. Which mystery was hidden or concealed in God, that is, in the knowledge of the divine Mind, from the ages, that is, from the beginnings of all generations, namely from the origin of the world, so that it was not fully manifested to any creature, angelic or human. [[3:9|who created all things|Qui Deus omnia creavit]], that is, God. [[3:10|That the manifold wisdom of God may be made known to the principalities and powers in heavenly places through the church|Ut innotescat principibus et potestatibus in cœlestibus per Ecclesiam multiformis sapientia Dei]], [[3:11|According to the eternal purpose which he made in Christ Jesus our Lord|secundum præfinitionem sæculorum, quam fecit Deus in Christo Jesu Domino nostro]], God having made it.

paras.t: In horum expositione verborum maximam difficultatem habentium, S. Hieronymus et Augustinus non nihil dissonare videntur. Secundum Hieronymum enim exponitur sic : Mihi data est gratia evangelizare in gentibus investigabiles divitias Christi, ut innotescat, id est, ita ut notificetur, principibus et potestatibus, id est angelorum ordinibus qui sunt in cœlestibus mansionibus, per Ecclesiam, id est per Apostolorum in Ecclesia prædicationem, seu ex prædicatione Apostolorum in Ecclesiis facta, multiformis sapientia Dei, id est divinæ mentis sapientialis dispositio de humani generis liberatione. Quæ utique cognitio vel sapientia Dei, quamvis in se una et simplicissima sit, tamen propter diversa quæ includit, concernit et efficit, multiformis vocatur. Est enim de omnibus mysteriis Christi. — Quod autem subjungitur, Secundum præfinitionem sæculorum, etc., referri potest ad verbum, Innotescat. Eritque sensus : Ut innotescat principibus et potestatibus per Apostolorum prædicationem multiformis sapientia Dei, secundum præfinitionem sæculorum, id est secundum prædicationem dominicam ab exordio temporum præconceptam : quam præordinationem fecit, id est effectui mancipavit, in Christo Jesu Domino nostro, id est per Christi prædicationem inchoative, et per missionem ac illuminationem qua ipse Apostolos docuit, et ad prædicationem emisit. — Secundo refertur ad nomen, Multiformis. Tanquam dicat : Multiformis sapientia Dei, non in se multiformis, sed simplex ; multiformis vero, secundum præfinitionem sæculorum, id est secundum ordinationem eorum quæ in sæculo fiunt, vel secundum hæc ipsa ex divina præordinatione procedentia : quam præfinitionem fecit, id est implevit, vel implere disposuit, Deus Pater in Christo Jesu Domino nostro, id est per unigenitum Filium suum, per quem facta sunt omnia; qui testatur : Pater meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor.
paras.en: In expounding these words, which have the greatest difficulty, St Jerome and Augustine seem to differ somewhat. According to Jerome it is expounded thus: [[3:8|is given this grace, to preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ|Mihi data est gratia evangelizare in gentibus investigabiles divitias Christi]], [[3:10|That the manifold wisdom of God may be made known|ut innotescat]], that is, so that there be made known [[3:10|to the principalities and powers|principibus et potestatibus]], that is, to the orders of angels who are [[3:10|in heavenly places|in cœlestibus]], in the heavenly mansions, [[3:10|through the church|per Ecclesiam]], that is, through the preaching of the Apostles in the Church, or from the preaching of the Apostles made in the churches, [[3:10|the manifold wisdom of God|multiformis sapientia Dei]], that is, the wise disposition of the divine Mind concerning the deliverance of mankind. This knowledge or wisdom of God, though in itself one and most simple, is yet called manifold because of the diverse things it includes, concerns and effects; for it is of all the mysteries of Christ. — What is added, According to the eternal purpose [præfinitio sæculorum: literally the predetermination of the ages], etc., can be referred to the verb, may be made known. And the sense will be: That the manifold wisdom of God may be made known to the principalities and powers through the preaching of the Apostles, [[3:11|According to the eternal purpose|secundum præfinitionem sæculorum]], that is, according to the Lord's preaching conceived beforehand from the beginning of time: [[3:11|which he made|quam præordinationem fecit]], which preordination he brought into effect, [[3:11|in Christ Jesus our Lord|in Christo Jesu Domino nostro]], that is, through Christ's preaching as a beginning, and through the sending and enlightening by which he taught the Apostles and sent them out to preach. — Secondly, it is referred to the noun, manifold. As if he said: The manifold wisdom of God, not manifold in itself, but simple; yet manifold according to the eternal purpose, that is, according to the ordering of the things done in the world, or according to these very things proceeding from the divine preordination: which purpose God the Father made, that is, fulfilled, or disposed to fulfil, in Christ Jesus our Lord, that is, through his only-begotten Son, by whom [[John 1:3|All things were made by him|per quem facta sunt omnia]]; who testifies: [[John 5:17|My Father worketh until now; and I work|Pater meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor]].

paras.t: Secundo exponitur, juxta Augustinum, hoc modo : Mihi data est gratia illuminare omnes, quæ sit dispensatio sacramenti absconditi a sæculis in Deo, ut innotescat, id est, sic tamen ut innotuerit, principibus et potestatibus, id est angelis universis, per Ecclesiam, id est in Ecclesia, multiformis sapientia Dei. Ponit ergo Augustinus super Genesim, quod omnes angeli, a principio sæculi præcognoverunt mysterium regni cœlestis, id est unigeniti Filii Dei incarnationem. Quod etiam Thomas in prima parte affirmat, rationem adjiciens : Quoniam incarnatio Verbi, est finis ad quem omnia angelorum ministeria ordinantur. Omnes autem sunt aliquo modo administratorii spiritus. Omnes ergo sacramentum hoc cognoverunt quantum ad substantiam ejus in generali, non autem quantum ad singulas circumstantias seu particulares conditiones ipsius. Et quantum ad hoc, profecerunt in cognitione multiformis sapientiæ Dei mysteriorumque Christi, tempore ascensionis et prædicationis Apostolorum. Porro, B. Hieronymus videtur sentire oppositum hoc loco, et in Isaia, exponens illud, Quis est iste qui venit de Edom ? Ait itaque, quod angeli mysterium incarnationis passionisque Christi ignoraverunt, donec impleretur, a Christo quoque ascendente illud addiscerent, atque ex prædicatione Apostolorum in ejus agnitione proficerent. Verumtamen si dicta Hieronymi diligenter inspiciantur, non videntur prædictis penitus dissonare. Nam asserit, quod angelicæ dignitates non ad purum intellexerunt præmemoratum mysterium, donec completa est passio Christi, et Apostolorum prædicatio in gentes promulgata. Certum est autem dici non posse, quod angeli absolute nescierunt mysteria Christi, donec rebus essent expleta. Propheticæ autem revelationes, secundum Dionysium, angelorum ministerio fiunt. Quod ergo de Christo præcognoverunt Prophetæ, angeli prius certiusque noverunt. — De hac vero materia plenius dixi in Isaia, exponendo capitulum illud, cujus exordium est : Quis est iste qui venit de Edom ? Videtur quoque expositio gloriosi Hieronymi hoc loco magis concordare litteræ, quam expositio Augustini, ut constat inspicienti.
paras.en: Secondly it is expounded, following Augustine, in this way: To me is given grace [[3:9|to enlighten all men, that they may see what is the dispensation of the mystery which hath been hidden from eternity in God|illuminare omnes, quæ sit dispensatio sacramenti absconditi a sæculis in Deo]], [[3:10|That the manifold wisdom of God may be made known|ut innotescat]], that is, yet in such a way that it had become known, [[3:10|to the principalities and powers|principibus et potestatibus]], that is, to all the angels, [[3:10|through the church|per Ecclesiam]], that is, in the Church, [[3:10|the manifold wisdom of God|multiformis sapientia Dei]]. Augustine therefore holds, on Genesis, that all the angels from the beginning of the world foreknew the mystery of the kingdom of heaven, that is, the incarnation of the only-begotten Son of God. Thomas too affirms this in the First Part, adding the reason: since the incarnation of the Word is the end to which all the ministries of the angels are ordered; and all are in some way ministering spirits[[Heb 1:14||]]. All, then, knew this mystery as to its substance in general, but not as to its several circumstances or particular conditions; and in this respect they advanced in the knowledge of the manifold wisdom of God and of the mysteries of Christ at the time of the ascension and of the preaching of the Apostles. Blessed Jerome, however, seems to hold the opposite here, and in Isaias, expounding the words [[Is 63:1|Who is this that cometh from Edom|Quis est iste qui venit de Edom]]? He says that the angels were ignorant of the mystery of Christ's incarnation and passion until it was fulfilled, and learned it from Christ as he ascended, and advanced in the knowledge of it from the preaching of the Apostles. Yet if Jerome's words are examined carefully, they do not seem wholly at odds with what has been said. For he asserts that the angelic dignities did not understand the aforesaid mystery purely [that is, clearly and in full] until the passion of Christ was completed and the preaching of the Apostles published among the nations. It is certain, however, that it cannot be said that the angels were absolutely ignorant of the mysteries of Christ until they were accomplished in fact. For prophetic revelations, according to Dionysius, are made by the ministry of angels; what, then, the Prophets foreknew of Christ, the angels knew earlier and more surely. — I have spoken more fully of this matter in Isaias, expounding the chapter that begins: [[Is 63:1|Who is this that cometh from Edom|Quis est iste qui venit de Edom]]? The exposition of the glorious Jerome also seems in this place to agree better with the letter than Augustine's, as is plain to anyone who looks.

paras.t: In quo Christo, id est cujus gratia et merito, habemus fiduciam futuræ felicitatis, et accessum ad Deum in confidentia, id est confidendo de bonitate Dei, meritis Christi et actibus propriis, per fidem ejus, quia in fide Christi omnia bona nostra fundantur. Unde et confidentia ista ex fide procedit.
paras.en: [[3:12|In whom|In quo]], Christ, that is, by whose grace and merit, [[3:12|we have boldness|habemus fiduciam]] of the happiness to come, [[3:12|and access|et accessum]] to God [[3:12|with confidence|in confidentia]], that is, trusting in the goodness of God, in the merits of Christ and in our own acts, [[3:12|by the faith of him|per fidem ejus]], because all our goods are founded in the faith of Christ. Hence this confidence too proceeds from faith.

paras.t: Consequenter admonet Ephesios ad patientiam atque constantiam. Propter quod obsecro, id est, per sacra vos rogo, ne deficiatis, id est, ne frangamini per impatientiam, pusillanimitatem, aut tædium animi, nec a fide bonoque opere desistatis, in tribulationibus meis, id est ex consideratione persecutionum et adversitatum quas patior pro vobis, hoc est ad vestri ædificationem ac probationem; quæ constantia, scilicet non deficere, est gloria vestra, id est gloriosum meritum vestrum. Solent autem pusilli scandalizari, frangi, deficere, dum conspiciunt justos ab impiis opprimi aut occidi. In quorum persona scriptum est ab Habacuc : Quare, Domine, non respicis contemptores, et taces conculcante impio justiorem se? Propter hoc lacerata est lex. Exercitati autem in via et lege divina, qui sciunt quod per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum cœleste, et quod pœnæ justorum in hac vita non sunt nisi medicinæ atque remedia, non moventur ex hoc ; quin potius dicunt illud Salvatoris : Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cælorum.
paras.en: Next he exhorts the Ephesians to patience and constancy. [[3:13|Wherefore I pray you|Propter quod obsecro]], that is, I beg you by holy things, [[3:13|not to faint|ne deficiatis]], that is, not to be broken by impatience, faint-heartedness or weariness of mind, nor to desist from faith and good works, [[3:13|at my tribulations|in tribulationibus meis]], that is, from considering the persecutions and adversities which I suffer [[3:13|for you|pro vobis]], that is, for your edification and proving; [[3:13|which is your glory|quæ est gloria vestra]]: which constancy, namely not fainting, is your glorious merit. Now the little ones are wont to be scandalized, broken and to faint when they see the just oppressed or slain by the wicked. In their person it is written by Habacuc: Why, O Lord, dost thou not look upon the despisers, and [[Hab 1:13|holdest thy peace when the wicked devoureth the man that is more just than himself?|et taces conculcante impio justiorem se]]? [[Hab 1:4|Therefore the law is torn in pieces|Propter hoc lacerata est lex]] [the margin gives Hab. i, 13, 3, as a loose citation; the last words are from Hab 1:4]. But those trained in the way and law of God, who know that [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom|per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum]] of heaven, and that the punishments of the just in this life are nothing but medicines and remedies, are not moved by this; rather they say with the Saviour: [[Matt 5:10|Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.|Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam: quoniam ipsorum est regnum cælorum.]]

paras.t: Hujus rei gratia, puta, ne deficiatis a bono propter adversa, flecto genua mea, corpus in oratione humiliando, ad insinuandam vel excitandam cordis mei humiliationem, ad Patrem Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ex quo omnis paternitas in cælis et in terra nominatur, id est, de cujus verissima paternitate derivatur et nomen paternitatis sortitur omnis paternitas angelorum et hominum : ita quod paternitas primo et proprie convenit Deo Patri, qui genuit Filium, non solum in natura similem, sed etiam sibi consubstantialem; ceteris vero convenit paternitas per quamdam imitationem paternitatis divinæ. Ut det vobis secundum divitias gloriæ suæ, id est secundum plenitudinem suæ perfectionis increatæ et opulentissimæ, virtutem, id est cordis constantiam, corroborari, id est, ut confirmemini, per Spiritum ejus, id est per inspirationem et opem Spiritus Sancti, in interiori homine, id est in anima : quod est habitare Christum per fidem formatam in cordibus vestris, id est mansionem quietam ac jugem præsidentiam habere in interioribus vestris. Sitis quoque in caritate Dei ac proximi radicati, id est radicitus fixi, seu firmiter inhærentes, quemadmodum radix terræ fortiter inest, et fundati, id est per firmas rationes divini amoris stabiliti, videlicet ex consideratione divinæ bonitatis in se, et caritatis ejus super nos, ex consideratione etiam beneficiorum promissionumque Christi :
paras.en: [[3:14|For this cause|Hujus rei gratia]], namely, that you may not faint from good because of adversity, [[3:14|I bow my knees|flecto genua mea]], humbling the body in prayer to show forth or stir up the humbling of my heart, [[3:14|to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ|ad Patrem Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], [[3:15|Of whom all paternity in heaven and earth is named:|ex quo omnis paternitas in cælis et in terra nominatur,]], that is, from whose most true paternity all paternity of angels and men is derived and takes the name of paternity: so that paternity belongs first and properly to God the Father, who begot a Son not only like in nature but also consubstantial with himself; while to others paternity belongs by a certain imitation of the divine paternity. [[3:16|That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory|Ut det vobis secundum divitias gloriæ suæ]], that is, according to the fulness of his uncreated and most opulent perfection, might [virtutem], that is, constancy of heart, [[3:16|to be strengthened|corroborari]], that is, that you be confirmed, [[3:16|by his Spirit|per Spiritum ejus]], that is, by the inspiration and help of the Holy Ghost, [[3:16|unto the inward man|in interiori homine]], that is, in the soul: which is [[3:17|That Christ may dwell by faith|habitare Christum per fidem]] formed [that is, faith informed by charity] [[3:17|in your hearts|in cordibus vestris]], that is, have a quiet mansion and continual presidency within you. Be also, [[3:17|in charity|in caritate]] of God and neighbour, [[3:17|being rooted|radicati]], that is, fixed by the roots, or firmly cleaving, as a root is strongly set in the earth, [[3:17|and founded|et fundati]], that is, established by firm reasons of divine love, namely from considering the divine goodness in itself and his charity towards us, and also from considering the benefits and promises of Christ:

paras.t: Ut possitis comprehendere, id est sincere cognoscere, cum omnibus sanctis, id est, sicut sancti in via Deo revelante cognoscunt, quæ sit latitudo spiritualis caritatis, et longitudo, et sublimitas, et profundum ejus. Hæ dimensiones attribuuntur caritati, per similitudinem corporalium dimensionum. Unde latitudo caritatis est quod ad omnes extenditur, etiam inimicos. Longitudo ejus est, quod tendit in longum atque futurum, videlicet usque in ultimum finem, seu vitam æternam, nec frangitur propter dilationem. Unde secundum Augustinum, longitudo est perseverandi longanimitas. Sublimitas vero caritatis est, quod immediate unit nos Deo, imo in Deum transformat, eique inseparabiliter colligat : quod maxime in patria adimpletur. Profundum autem caritatis est, condescensus ad proximum, vel humiliationis declivitas ex consideratione terribilium judiciorum Dei. — Possunt quoque hæc quatuor metaphorice ad divinam referri naturam : ut latitudo pertineat ad divinæ naturæ communicabilitatem, qua Deus dat omnibus affluenter, nec aliquid expers est a divinæ bonitatis participatione ; longitudo vero pertineat ad æternitatem, qua attingit a fine usque ad finem, imo universa præcedit et omnia sequitur, vel ad longanimem exspectationem qua impiorum præstolatur emendationem; sublimitas autem ad majestatis divinæ incircumscriptibilem excellentiam, vel ad promissorum supernaturalem dignitatem; profundum quoque ad incomprehensibilia divinæ naturæ, ejusque judiciorum, de quibus dicit Scriptura : Judicia tua abyssus multa ; item alibi : Excelsior cælo est, et quid facies? profundior inferno, et unde cognosces? Longior terra mensura ejus, et latior mari.
paras.en: [[3:18|You may be able to comprehend|Ut possitis comprehendere]], that is, truly to know, [[3:18|with all the saints|cum omnibus sanctis]], that is, as the saints on the way [that is, in this life] know by God's revealing, [[3:18|what is the breadth|quæ sit latitudo]] of spiritual charity, [[3:18|and length and height and depth|et longitudo, et sublimitas, et profundum]] of it. These dimensions are attributed to charity by likeness to bodily dimensions. So the breadth of charity is that it extends to all, even enemies. Its length is that it reaches far into the future, namely to the last end, or eternal life, and is not broken by delay; hence according to Augustine, length is the long-suffering of perseverance. The height of charity is that it unites us immediately to God, nay transforms us into God and binds us inseparably to him: which is fulfilled most of all in the fatherland. The depth of charity is condescension to the neighbour, or the downward slope of humility from considering the terrible judgments of God. — These four can also be referred metaphorically to the divine nature: breadth to the communicability of the divine nature, by which God [[Jas 1:5|giveth to all men abundantly|dat omnibus affluenter]], and nothing is without a share in the divine goodness; length to eternity, by which he [[Wis 8:1|reacheth therefore from end to end|attingit a fine usque ad finem]], nay goes before all things and follows all, or to the long-suffering waiting with which he awaits the amendment of the wicked; height to the uncircumscribable excellence of the divine majesty, or to the supernatural dignity of the things promised; depth to the incomprehensible things of the divine nature and of his judgments, of which Scripture says: [[Ps 35:7|thy judgments are a great deep|Judicia tua abyssus multa]]; and elsewhere: [[Job 11:8|He is higher than heaven, and what wilt thou do? he is deeper than hell, and how wilt thou know?|Excelsior cælo est, et quid facies? profundior inferno, et unde cognosces?]] [[Job 11:9|The measure of him is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.|Longior terra mensura ejus, et latior mari.]]

paras.t: Possitis scire etiam scientia practica, id est sciendo imitari et juste agere, supereminentem scientiæ caritatem Christi, id est dilectionem illam præcipuam qua Christus secundum suam scientiam nos dilexit. Dilectio enim ex cognitione procedit. Vel sic : Possitis scire caritatem Christi supereminentem scientiæ, id est nostram notitiam sua magnitudine excedentem. Ut impleamini, id est, divinarum gratiarum recipiendo influxum, tendatis ac perducamini, in omnem plenitudinem Dei, id est ad omnia dona perfecta quæ conferuntur a Deo, quatenus nunc obtineatis plenitudinem meritorum, postmodum vero plenitudinem præmiorum.
paras.en: May you be able [[3:19|To know also|scire etiam]] with practical knowledge, that is, by knowing to imitate and act justly, [[3:19|the charity of Christ, which surpasseth all knowledge|supereminentem scientiæ caritatem Christi]], that is, that singular love with which Christ loved us according to his knowledge; for love proceeds from knowledge. Or thus: may you be able to know the charity of Christ surpassing knowledge, that is, exceeding our understanding by its greatness. [[3:19|that you may be filled|Ut impleamini]], that is, receiving the inflowing of divine graces, may tend and be brought [[3:19|unto all the fulness of God|in omnem plenitudinem Dei]], that is, to all the perfect gifts conferred by God, so that now you may obtain the fulness of merits, and afterwards the fulness of rewards.

paras.t: Ei autem, scilicet Deo omnipotenti, qui potens est omnia sibi placentia et nobis salubria facere, id est implere, superabundanter quam petimus aut intelligimus, id est copiosius quam orare aut nosse valeamus, qui tamen plus intelligimus quam orare præsumamus, secundum virtutem, id est omnipotentiam suam, quæ operatur in nobis ut causa prima ac principalis, nobisque virtutem et gratiam operandi largitur; ipsi sit gloria, id est clara cum laude notitia, in Ecclesia, id est in cordibus fidelium qui Deum glorificant, et in Christo Jesu, id est propter ea quæ nobis per Christum donavit : gloria, inquam, duratura in omnes generationes, id est per universa generationum intervalla seu tempora, sæculi, id est præsentis vitæ contentivæ sæculorum, id est includentis in se sæcula universa, id est singulas mundi ætates. Porro, secundum Damascenum, sæculum multa significat : primo, uniuscujusque rei vitam; secundo, tempus mille annorum; tertio, totam vitam, seu durationem (ut ita loquar) præsentem; quarto, vitam futuram in patria post resurrectionem novissimam; quinto, mensuram æternorum; sexto, mensuram perpetuorum; septimo, singulas septem mundi ætates. Amen.
paras.en: [[3:20|Now to him|Ei autem]], namely to almighty God, [[3:20|who is able to do all things|qui potens est omnia]] pleasing to him and wholesome for us [[3:20|to do|facere]], that is, to fulfil, [[3:20|more abundantly than we desire or understand|superabundanter quam petimus aut intelligimus]], that is, more plentifully than we are able to pray or to know, we who yet understand more than we presume to pray for, [[3:20|according to the power|secundum virtutem]], that is, his omnipotence, [[3:20|that worketh in us|quæ operatur in nobis]] as first and principal cause, and bestows on us the power and grace of working; [[3:21|To him be glory|ipsi sit gloria]], that is, clear knowledge with praise, [[3:21|in the church|in Ecclesia]], that is, in the hearts of the faithful who glorify God, [[3:21|and in Christ Jesus|et in Christo Jesu]], that is, for the things he has given us through Christ: glory, I say, to last [[3:21|unto all generations|in omnes generationes]], that is, through all the spans or times of the generations, of the world [sæculi], that is, of the present life which contains the ages, [sæculorum] of ages, that is, which includes in itself all the ages, namely the several ages of the world. Now according to Damascene, *sæculum* signifies many things: first, the life of each thing; second, a period of a thousand years; third, the whole present life or duration (so to speak); fourth, the life to come in the fatherland after the last resurrection; fifth, the measure of eternal things; sixth, the measure of perpetual things; seventh, each of the seven ages of the world. [[3:21|Amen|Amen]].

4.title: DECLARATIO CAPITULI QUARTI : OBSECRO ITAQUE VOS EGO VINCTUS IN DOMINO.
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: I therefore, a prisoner in the Lord, beseech you.

paras.t: Docuit sanctus Apostolus omnia bona nostra divinæ pietati ac gratiæ esse adscribenda; induxit quoque Ephesios ad gratiarum actionem, et fudit pro eis precem devotam. Jam in moralibus instruit eos, dicendo: Obsecro itaque vos ego vinctus, id est Romæ incarceratus atque ligatus, in Domino, id est propter Deum et fidei prædicationem, ut digne ambuletis, quotidie in virtutibus proficiendo: digne, inquam, vocatione qua vocati estis ad christianam religionem atque evangelicam legem, me foris per prædicationem meam vocante, Deo autem interius operante et per inspirationem internam vocante: hoc est, sic vivite ut convenit Christianis, et sicut lex jubet quam assumpsistis:
paras.en: The holy Apostle has taught that all our good things are to be ascribed to the divine goodness and grace; he has also moved the Ephesians to give thanks, and has poured out a devout prayer for them. Now he instructs them in morals, saying: [[4:1|I therefore|Obsecro itaque]] [[4:1|beseech you|vos]], [[4:1|a prisoner|ego vinctus]], that is, imprisoned and bound at Rome, [[4:1|in the Lord|in Domino]], that is, for God's sake and for the preaching of the faith, [[4:1|that you walk worthy|ut digne ambuletis]], advancing daily in the virtues: worthy, I say, [[4:1|of the vocation in which you are called|vocatione qua vocati estis]] to the Christian religion and the law of the Gospel, I calling you outwardly by my preaching, and God working within and calling you by inward inspiration: that is, live as befits Christians, and as the law you have taken upon you commands:

paras.t: Cum omni humilitate interiori et exteriori in verbis et factis, ita ut latentem superbiam et manifestam præsumptionem ac pompam abjiciatis, et mansuetudine, id est mititate iram refrenante. Hoc et Christus admonet: Discite (inquiens) a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde. Unde et Tobias præcepit filio suo: Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu aut in verbo tuo dominari permittas; in ipsa enim sumpsit initium omnis perditio. Et in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Odibilis coram Deo et hominibus est superbia. De commendatione vero mansuetudinis scriptum est: Fili, in mansuetudine opera tua perfice, et super hominum gloriam diligeris. Cum patientia, quæ passionem tristitiæ aufert, id est cum æquanimi tolerantia adversorum. Supportantes invicem mutuos defectus atque labores, compatiendo peccantibus et laborantibus succurrendo, sicut alibi dictum est: Alter alterius onera portate; in caritate, id est sincero affectu, non simulatione aut pro commodo temporali; solliciti servare, id est studiosi ac diligentes ad conservandum, unitatem spiritus, id est spiritualem unionem et conformitatem animorum, ut sit vobis anima una per caritatis affectum; vel, Unitatem spiritus, id est unitatem Ecclesiæ quam facit Spiritus Sanctus; in vinculo pacis, id est in pace seu tranquillitate animi, quæ est spirituale vinculum unitatis præfatæ, quoniam nutrit eam atque conservat.
paras.en: [[4:2|With all humility|Cum omni humilitate]], inward and outward, in words and deeds, so that you cast away hidden pride and open presumption and display; [[4:2|and mildness|et mansuetudine]], that is, with meekness reining in anger. Christ too admonishes this, saying: [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|Discite (inquiens) a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]. Hence Tobias also commanded his son: [[Tob 4:14|Never suffer pride to reign in thy mind, or in thy words: for from it all perdition took its beginning|Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu aut in verbo tuo dominari permittas; in ipsa enim sumpsit initium omnis perditio]]. And in Ecclesiasticus it is written: [[Ecclus 10:7|Pride is hateful before God and men|Odibilis coram Deo et hominibus est superbia]]. And in praise of meekness it is written: [[Ecclus 3:19|My son, do thy works in meekness, and thou shalt be beloved above the glory of men.|Fili, in mansuetudine opera tua perfice, et super hominum gloriam diligeris]] [[4:2|With patience|Cum patientia]], which takes away the passion of sadness, that is, with even-minded bearing of adversities. [[4:2|Supporting one another|Supportantes invicem]] in your mutual failings and labours, by suffering with those who sin and helping those who labour, as is said elsewhere: [[Gal 6:2|Bear ye one another's burdens|Alter alterius onera portate]]; [[4:2|in charity|in caritate]], that is, with sincere affection, not in pretence or for temporal advantage; [[4:3|Careful to keep|solliciti servare]], that is, zealous and diligent in preserving, [[4:3|the unity of the Spirit|unitatem spiritus]], that is, the spiritual union and agreement of minds, so that you may have one soul through the affection of charity[[Acts 4:32||]]; or, The unity of the Spirit, that is, the unity of the Church, which the Holy Ghost makes[[John 17:21||]]; [[4:3|in the bond of peace|in vinculo pacis]], that is, in peace or tranquillity of mind, which is the spiritual bond of the aforesaid unity, since it nourishes and preserves it.

paras.t: Unum corpus Christi mysticum estis, et unus spiritus cum Deo, ei fideliter adhærendo; vel, Unus spiritus cum spiritu Christi per caritatem, eadem volendo ac nolendo cum eo, quemadmodum per Jeremiam Dominus loquitur: Dabo eis cor unum et animam unam; sicut vocati estis in unam spem, id est ad eamdem beatitudinem sperandam, vocationis vestræ, id est ad quam vestra vocatio ordinatur.
paras.en: You are [[4:4|One body|Unum corpus]], the mystical body of Christ[[Rom 12:5||]], [[4:4|and one Spirit|et unus spiritus]] with God, by cleaving faithfully to him[[1 Cor 6:17||]]; or, One spirit with the spirit of Christ through charity, by willing and not willing the same things as he, as the Lord says by Jeremias: [[Jer 32:39|I will give them one heart|Dabo eis cor unum]], and one soul [the Vulgate has "and one way"; Denis's "one soul" recalls Acts 4:32]; [[4:4|as you are called in one hope|sicut vocati estis in unam spem]], that is, to hope for the same beatitude, [[4:4|of your calling|vocationis vestræ]], that is, to which your calling is ordered.

paras.t: Merito insuper observanda est unitas ista interna ac spiritualis: nam, Unus Dominus, scilicet Deus Trinitas. De quo in libro Esther legitur: Domine, rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita. Una fides in specie ex parte objecti, quod est veritas prima; sed ex parte subjectorum fides numeraliter diversificatur. Quamvis enim multa sint credenda et multi articuli fidei, una tamen est formalis et propria ratio objectalis, propter quam omnibus creditur, et cui fides innitur, scilicet veritas increata. Unum Baptisma in specie, quia materia una est, utpote aqua, et forma Baptismi eadem est. Vel dicitur Baptisma unum, ex parte interioris baptistæ, videlicet Christi, qui solus lavat et mundat interius. Vel ideo unum vocatur, quia iterari non potest, estque ejusdem valoris a quocumque ministretur, quoniam non consistit in merito dantis, sed in virtute dominicæ passionis.
paras.en: Moreover, this inward and spiritual unity is rightly to be kept: for there is [[4:5|One Lord|Unus Dominus]], namely God the Trinity, of whom we read in the book of Esther: O Lord, [[Esth 13:9|almighty king|rex omnipotens]], [[Esth 13:9|all things are in thy power|in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita]]. [[4:5|one faith|Una fides]], one in species on the side of the object, which is the first truth; but on the side of the subjects [that is, the believers] faith is diversified in number. For though there are many things to be believed and many articles of faith, there is yet one formal and proper objective reason [that is, the one ground in the object for which assent is given], on account of which all of them are believed and on which faith rests, namely the uncreated truth. [[4:5|one baptism|Unum Baptisma]], one in species, because its matter is one, namely water, and the form of Baptism is the same. Or Baptism is called one on the side of the inward baptizer, namely Christ, who alone washes and cleanses within. Or it is called one because it cannot be repeated, and it is of the same worth by whomsoever it is ministered, since it does not rest on the merit of the giver but on the power of the Lord's passion.

paras.t: Unus Deus et Pater omnium, id est Deus Trinitas: qui Deus dicitur propter creationem; Pater, propter benignam gubernationem; qui est super omnes, id est incomparabili dignitate cunctis præstantior, et per omnia spiritualiter extentus sive diffusus, cunctaque penetrans et includens: propter quod per Jeremiam contestatur: Numquid non cælum et terram ego impleo? et […] omnibus eorum credentibus atque electis est per […], caritatem et gratiam.
paras.en: [[4:6|One God and Father of all|Unus Deus et Pater omnium]], that is, God the Trinity, who is called God by reason of creation, and Father by reason of his kindly governance; [[4:6|who is above all|qui est super omnes]], that is, more excellent than all things in incomparable dignity, [[4:6|and through all|et per omnia]], spiritually extended or spread abroad, and penetrating and enclosing all things: for which reason he declares by Jeremias: [[Jer 23:24|do not I fill heaven and earth|Numquid non cælum et terram ego impleo]]? and […] all of them that believe and are elect, he is through […], charity and grace.

paras.t: Sed ne ex hoc quod dixit nos esse unum corpus unumque spiritum, æstimetur in omnibus esse par gratia, subditur: Unicuique autem nostrum data est gratia gratum faciens, vel gratis data, seu utraque simul, secundum mensuram donationis Christi, id est juxta quantitatem mensuratam a Christo, vel secundum quod Christus dator mensurat, qui dat singulis secundum propriam capacitatem sive virtutem.
paras.en: But lest, from his having said that we are one body and one spirit, it be thought that grace is equal in all, he adds: [[4:7|But to every one of us is given grace|Unicuique autem nostrum data est gratia]], sanctifying grace or grace freely given [that is, *gratia gratum faciens*, which makes the soul pleasing to God, or *gratia gratis data*, a gift such as prophecy given for the good of others], or both together, [[4:7|according to the measure of the giving of Christ|secundum mensuram donationis Christi]], that is, according to the amount measured out by Christ, or according as Christ the giver measures it, who gives to each according to his own capacity or strength.

paras.t: Propter quod dicit Psalmista: Ascendens Christus in altum, id est in cœlum empyreum in die ascensionis, captivam duxit captivitatem, id est, a diabolo captos eripuit, cepit, et secum deduxit, videlicet Sanctos de limbo, omnesque omnino purgatos; dedit dona hominibus, maxime in die sancto Pentecostes, quando discipulis mittens Spiritum Sanctum, implevit corda eorum diversis charismatibus Spiritus Sancti, ut patet in Actibus. Allegat autem Apostolus potius sensum quam verba Psalmistæ. Sic enim continet nostra translatio: Ascendisti in altum, cepisti captivitatem, accepisti dona in hominibus.
paras.en: [[4:8|Wherefore he saith|Propter quod dicit]], namely the Psalmist: Christ, [[4:8|Ascending on high|Ascendens Christus in altum]], that is, into the empyrean heaven on the day of the ascension, [[4:8|he led captivity captive|captivam duxit captivitatem]], that is, he snatched away those taken captive by the devil, took them, and led them away with him, namely the Saints from limbo and all who were wholly purged; [[4:8|he gave gifts to men|dedit dona hominibus]], above all on the holy day of Pentecost[[Acts 2:1||]], when, sending the Holy Ghost to the disciples, he filled their hearts with the various charisms of the Holy Ghost, as is plain in the Acts. Now the Apostle cites the sense rather than the words of the Psalmist; for our translation reads thus: [[Ps 67:19|Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive; thou hast received gifts in men|Ascendisti in altum, cepisti captivitatem, accepisti dona in hominibus]].

paras.t: Quod autem Christus ascendit, quid est, id est, quomodo verum est, nisi quia et descendit primum, id est ante, videlicet in die resurrectionis seu mortis suæ, in inferiores partes terræ, id est ad limbum patrum, qui est secus infernum situm in medio terræ? Inde enim captivam duxit captivitatem. Porro Christus in puncto mortis suæ descendit in limbum, quantum ad animam: in die vero resurrectionis rediit illuc cum corpore et anima, secundum quosdam. Vel sic: Descendit primum in inferiores partes terræ, id est ad hunc mundum inferiorem, humanam naturam assumendo, atque in mundo visibiliter operando. Inde ipse ait: Nemo ascendit in cœlum, nisi qui descendit de cœlo.
paras.en: [[4:9|Now that he ascended|Quod autem Christus ascendit]], namely Christ, [[4:9|what is it|quid est]], that is, how is it true, [[4:9|but because he also descended first|nisi quia et descendit primum]], that is, before, namely on the day of his resurrection or of his death, [[4:9|into the lower parts of the earth|in inferiores partes terræ]], that is, to the limbo of the fathers, which lies beside hell in the middle of the earth? For thence he led captivity captive. Christ, indeed, at the moment of his death went down into limbo as to his soul; but on the day of the resurrection, according to some, he returned there with body and soul. Or thus: He descended first into the lower parts of the earth, that is, to this lower world, by taking human nature and working visibly in the world. Hence he himself says: [[John 3:13|no man hath ascended into heaven, but he that descended from heaven|Nemo ascendit in cœlum, nisi qui descendit de cœlo]].

paras.t: Qui descendit modis præfatis, ipse […] in die ascensionis, se […] materiales et habitationes eorum. Ascendit autem loco et dignitate, vel potius dignitatis suæ manifestatione, super omnes creaturas corporales ac spirituales. Sunt autem septem cœli planetarum. Octavum cœlum, est firmamentum quod appellatur sidereum; estque partim diaphanum, et partim lucidum. Nonum, est cœlum crystallinum seu aqueum, omnino diaphanum, quod philosophi nominant nonam sphæram. Ultra quam aliqui ponunt decimam sphæram seu decimum cœlum, quod nominant primum mobile. Ultra hos cœlos est cœlum empyreum maxime uniforme ac simplex atque immobile, quod est mansio Beatorum. Denique, præter hos cœlos superiores, et secundum substantiam prorsus incorruptibiles, sunt cœli elementares, videlicet cœlum aerium, æthereum, olympium, et igneum. Sic ergo ascendit, ut impleret omnia quæ in lege, Prophetis ac Psalmis de ipso prænuntiata fuerunt. Unde in cruce dicebat: Consummatum est. Vel, Impleret omnia genera hominum, id est quosdam de universis generibus hominum, donis et gratiis Spiritus Sancti: de quibus omnibus dixit apud Joannem, Omnia traham ad me ipsum. Quomodo autem et quibus gradibus hoc fecerit, subditur:
paras.en: [[4:10|He that descended|Qui descendit]] in the ways aforesaid, [[4:10|the same|ipse]] […] on the day of the ascension, […] material […] and their dwellings. And he ascended in place and in dignity, or rather in the manifestation of his dignity, above all creatures, bodily and spiritual. Now there are seven heavens of the planets. The eighth heaven is the firmament, which is called starry; and it is partly transparent and partly luminous. The ninth is the crystalline or watery heaven, wholly transparent, which the philosophers call the ninth sphere. Beyond it some place a tenth sphere or tenth heaven, which they call the first movable [that is, the *primum mobile*, the outermost moving sphere that carries the others round]. Beyond these heavens is the empyrean heaven, supremely uniform, simple and unmoving, which is the dwelling of the Blessed. Lastly, besides these upper heavens, which are wholly incorruptible in their substance, there are the elemental heavens, namely the airy, ethereal, olympian and fiery heaven. Thus, then, he ascended [[4:10|that he might fill all things|ut impleret omnia]] that had been foretold of him in the law, the Prophets and the Psalms[[Luke 24:44||]]. Hence on the cross he said: [[John 19:30|It is consummated|Consummatum est]]. Or, That he might fill all kinds of men, that is, some of every kind of men, with the gifts and graces of the Holy Ghost: of all of whom he said in John: [[John 12:32|will draw all things to myself|Omnia traham ad me ipsum]]. And how, and by what degrees, he did this, is added:

paras.t: Et ipse Christus dedit, id est, gratis constituit, quosdam quidem Apostolos. De quibus in Luca habetur: Hos duodecim elegit, quos et Apostolos nominavit. Quosdam autem Prophetas, id est futurorum prænuntiatores: ut erant Agabus, et Dionysius, qui Joanni evangelistæ prophetavit de sua reductione a Patmos. Secundum Ambrosium, per prophetas potius intelliguntur Scripturarum expositores, quoniam in novo Testamento Scripturarum explanatores appellantur prophetæ. Alios vero Evangelistas: vel quia Evangelium conscripserunt, ut Lucas et Marcus, vel quia Evangelium prædicaverunt, ut septem diaconi et successores eorum. Evangelistæ namque vocantur, qui quamvis sacerdotes non sint, tamen evangelizare ex officio possunt. Alios autem dedit pastores et doctores, puta episcopos, qui verbo et opere gregem suum pascere habent. De qualibus Dominus loquitur per Jeremiam: Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina. Loquitur autem Apostolus de distinctione istorum formaliter. Materialiter namque frequenter coincidunt, eo quod eidem personæ diversæ gratiæ conferantur: nam ipsi Apostoli, utique et prophetæ et evangelistæ et pastores atque doctores fuerunt.
paras.en: [[4:11|And he|Et ipse]], Christ, [[4:11|gave|dedit]], that is, freely appointed, [[4:11|some apostles|quosdam quidem Apostolos]], of whom we read in Luke: [[Luke 6:13|he chose twelve of them (whom also he named apostles)|Hos duodecim elegit, quos et Apostolos nominavit]]. [[4:11|and some prophets|Quosdam autem Prophetas]], that is, foretellers of things to come, such as were Agabus[[Acts 11:28||]][[Acts 21:10||]], and Dionysius, who prophesied to John the evangelist of his return from Patmos. According to Ambrose, by prophets are rather to be understood expounders of the Scriptures, since in the New Testament those who explain the Scriptures are called prophets. [[4:11|and other some evangelists|Alios vero Evangelistas]]: either because they wrote the Gospel, as Luke and Mark, or because they preached the Gospel, as the seven deacons[[Acts 6:5||]] and their successors. For those are called evangelists who, though they are not priests, may yet preach the Gospel by their office. [[4:11|and other some pastors and doctors|Alios autem dedit pastores et doctores]], for example bishops, who have the duty of feeding their flock by word and deed. Of such the Lord speaks by Jeremias: [[Jer 3:15|I will give you pastors according to my own heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine|Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina]]. Now the Apostle speaks of the distinction of these formally [that is, as offices distinct in concept]; for materially [that is, in the persons who hold them] they often coincide, because diverse graces are conferred on the same person: for the Apostles themselves were also prophets, evangelists, pastors and doctors.

paras.t: Hos itaque dedit Deus ad consummationem sanctorum, id est, ut feliciter finiantur seu consummentur qui nunc sancti et perfecti consistunt, qui et a prædictis diriguntur in opus ministerii, id est operosum obsequium, puta ad hoc ut singuli sua officia ordinate et expedite valeant exsequi, in ædificationem corporis Christi, id est propter ædificationem spiritualem Ecclesiæ, et ut infideles ei per fidem incorporentur, quæ est mysticum corpus Christi.
paras.en: These, then, God gave [[4:12|For the perfecting of the saints|ad consummationem sanctorum]], that is, that those who are now holy and perfect may be happily brought to their end or consummation, who are also directed by the aforesaid for the work [[4:12|of the ministry|in opus ministerii]], that is, for busy service: for example, so that each may be able to carry out his own office in order and with readiness; [[4:12|for the edifying of the body of Christ|in ædificationem corporis Christi]], that is, for the spiritual building up of the Church, and so that unbelievers may be incorporated through faith into her who is the mystical body of Christ.

paras.t: Porro prælatio ordinationis prædictæ durabit, donec occurramus omnes, id est, in die judicii nobis invicem et Christo obviemus: juxta illud in Evangelio, Ecce sponsus venit, surgite obviam ei; et alibi, Simul rapiemur cum illis in nubibus obviam Christo; in unitatem fidei, id est, idem credentes, quantum ad electos fideles, qui nondum Deum per speciem videre meruerunt; et agnitionis, id est contemplationis, Filii Dei. Hoc refertur ad Beatos, qui ante futurum judicium Deo perfruuntur.
paras.en: Further, the prelacy of the aforesaid order will last [[4:13|Until we all meet|donec occurramus omnes]], that is, until on the day of judgment we meet one another and Christ: according to that saying in the Gospel, [[Matt 25:6|Behold the bridegroom cometh|Ecce sponsus venit]], arise to meet him [Denis reads *surgite*, arise, where the Vulgate has *exite*, go ye forth]; and elsewhere, We [[1 Thess 4:16|shall be taken up together with them in the clouds to meet Christ|Simul rapiemur cum illis in nubibus obviam Christo]]; [[4:13|into the unity of faith|in unitatem fidei]], that is, believing the same things, as regards the faithful elect who have not yet been found worthy to see God face to face; [[4:13|and of the knowledge|et agnitionis]], that is, the contemplation, [[4:13|of the Son of God|Filii Dei]]. This refers to the Blessed, who enjoy God before the judgment to come.

paras.t: Vel sic: Occurramus omnes, qui jam sumus et vivimus in unitate fidei, id est in una fide catholica, et agnitione fideli Christi Filii Dei. In virum perfectum, id est in statu perfecto, habentes videlicet perfectionem virtutum et fortitudinem animorum, sicque appareat nos esse viros, non ratione sexus, sed perfectionis. Non ergo ideo ait, In virum perfectum, quasi post resurrectionem defecturus sit sexus muliebris, sed quia electi feliciter immutabuntur. In mensuram ætatis plenitudinis Christi, id est, in ea ætate occurremus et resurgemus, qua Christus consummatus atque occisus est, scilicet in anno tricesimo tertio. Non ait, In mensuram corporis vel staturæ, quoniam unusquisque proprii corporis mensuram recipiet, quam vel in juventute habuit, licet senuerit, vel fuerat habiturus, nisi prius obiisset. Non autem satis est dicere, secundum Augustinum, quod in resurrectione detur corpori magnitudo quam non habuit, nec naturaliter habuisset, vel quod corpora majora ad dominici corporis quantitatem redigantur: sic enim multum periret de illis, quum tamen ne unus quidem periturus sit capillus eorum.
paras.en: Or thus: Let us all meet, we who already are and live in the unity of faith, that is, in the one Catholic faith, and in the faithful knowledge of Christ the Son of God. [[4:13|unto a perfect man|In virum perfectum]], that is, in a perfect state, having namely the perfection of the virtues and strength of soul; and so let it appear that we are men, not by reason of sex but of perfection. He does not therefore say, Unto a perfect man, as though after the resurrection the female sex were to fail, but because the elect will be happily changed[[1 Cor 15:51||]][[1 Cor 15:52||]]. [[4:13|unto the measure of the age of the fulness of Christ|In mensuram ætatis plenitudinis Christi]], that is, we shall meet him and rise again at that age at which Christ was perfected and slain, namely in his thirty-third year. He does not say, Unto the measure of the body or of the stature, since each one will receive the measure of his own body, which he either had in youth, though he grew old, or would have had if he had not died first. But it is not enough to say, according to Augustine, that in the resurrection the body is given a size it did not have and would not naturally have had, or that larger bodies are reduced to the size of the Lord's body: for so much of them would perish, whereas not even one hair of theirs is to perish[[Luke 21:18||]].

paras.t: Hæc vero tam præclara largitus sive daturus est Deus beneficia nobis, ut jam post receptionem Baptismi et conversionem nostram, non simus parvuli, id est discretione ac sensibus minorati seu modici, fluctuantes, id est instabiles, et circumferamur, id est, undique a Deo et rectitudine sanctæ conversationis abstrahamur ac evagemur, omni vento doctrinæ, id est inani, verbosa et turbulenta instructione hominum perversorum, ne deputemur cum illis, de quibus dicit Psalmista: In circuitu impii ambulant; et: Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam, et sicut stipulam ante faciem venti. Quæ circumferentia seu vana instructio fit in nequitia hominum, id est a nequam hominibus, in astutia, id est cum fraude et simulatione, ad circumventionem erroris, id est ad hoc ut alios fallant, mittendo eos in diversos errores sub prætextu justitiæ et specie veritatis.
paras.en: And God has bestowed, or will give, such splendid benefits on us, [[4:14|That henceforth|ut jam]], after receiving Baptism and after our conversion, [[4:14|we be no more children|non simus parvuli]], that is, lessened or small in discernment and senses, [[4:14|tossed to and fro|fluctuantes]], that is, unstable, [[4:14|and carried about|et circumferamur]], that is, drawn away on every side and straying from God and from the uprightness of holy living, [[4:14|with every wind of doctrine|omni vento doctrinæ]], that is, by the empty, wordy and turbulent instruction of perverse men; lest we be reckoned with those of whom the Psalmist says: [[Ps 11:9|The wicked walk round about|In circuitu impii ambulant]]; and: [[Ps 82:14|O my God, make them like a wheel; and as stubble before the wind.|Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam, et sicut stipulam ante faciem venti]] This carrying about, or vain instruction, is done [[4:14|by the wickedness of men|in nequitia hominum]], that is, by wicked men, [[4:14|by cunning craftiness|in astutia]], that is, with fraud and pretence, [[4:14|by which they lie in wait to deceive|ad circumventionem erroris]], that is, so as to deceive others, by sending them into divers errors under the pretext of justice and the appearance of truth.

paras.t: Veritatem autem justitiæ, id est opera justa, facientes, vel, Veritatem doctrinæ facientes, id est actibus virtuosis exsequentes, in caritate, id est ex caritatis impulsu atque imperio, non ficte, coacte aut formidolose: crescamus in gratia gratificante in illo per omnia virtutum exercitia, qui est caput nostrum, videlicet Christus, id est auxilio Christi secundum ejus consilia ad gloriam ejus:
paras.en: [[4:15|But doing the truth|Veritatem autem]] of justice, that is, doing just works; or, Doing the truth of doctrine, that is, carrying it out in virtuous acts, [[4:15|in charity|in caritate]], that is, from the impulse and command of charity, not feignedly, under constraint or in fear: let us [[4:15|grow up|crescamus]] in sanctifying grace [[4:15|in him|in illo]], [[4:15|in all things|per omnia]], that is, through all the exercises of the virtues, him [[4:15|who is the head|qui est caput nostrum]] of us, namely [[4:15|Christ|Christus]]: that is, by the help of Christ, according to his counsels, for his glory:

paras.t: ex quo, id est cujus virtute et operatione, totum corpus mysticum, quod est universa Ecclesia, compactum, id est per fidem et opera fortiter junctum, et connexum coagulo caritatis, per omnem juncturam subministrationis, id est per singula membra sive supposita, mysticum corpus integrantia, et sibi invicem caritative ministrantia, secundum operationem, id est realem et actualem subventionem seu servitutem, in mensuram uniuscujusque membri, id est juxta facultatem, proportionem, seu modum cuilibet personæ ecclesiasticæ convenientem, videlicet secundum quod gratia Dei in ea major aut minor est. Hoc itaque corpus ita compactum, augmentum corporis facit, id est, se ipsum auget ac perficit numero et merito per Christi virtutem, in ædificationem sui, id est ad hoc ut plures convertantur ad fidem, corrigantur in moribus, vel perficiantur virtutibus, in caritate, in qua tota spiritualis fundatur et consummatur constructio. Sic ergo corpus Ecclesiæ junctum est, ut singula membra ejus sibi invicem per dilectionem cohæreant atque ministrent.
paras.en: [[4:16|From whom|ex quo]], that is, by whose power and working, [[4:16|the whole body|totum corpus]], the mystical body, which is the whole Church, [[4:16|being compacted|compactum]], that is, strongly joined by faith and works, [[4:16|and fitly joined together|et connexum]] by the bond of charity, [[4:16|by what every joint supplieth|per omnem juncturam subministrationis]], that is, through the several members or persons [*supposita*] that make up the mystical body and minister to one another in charity, [[4:16|according to the operation|secundum operationem]], that is, real and actual help or service, [[4:16|in the measure of every part|in mensuram uniuscujusque membri]], that is, according to the ability, proportion or manner befitting each person in the Church, namely according as the grace of God in him is greater or less. This body, then, so compacted, [[4:16|maketh increase of the body|augmentum corporis facit]], that is, increases and perfects itself in number and in merit by the power of Christ, [[4:16|unto the edifying of itself|in ædificationem sui]], that is, so that more may be converted to the faith, corrected in their manners, or perfected in virtues, [[4:16|in charity|in caritate]], in which the whole spiritual building is founded and completed. Thus, then, the body of the Church is joined together, so that its several members cleave to one another through love and minister to one another[[Rom 12:5||]][[1 Cor 12:12||]][[1 Cor 12:25||]][[1 Cor 12:27||]].

paras.t: Consequenter instruuntur Ephesii in moribus, primoque admonentur declinare a malo. Hoc igitur, id est, quoniam tanta vobis collata est gratia, dico et testificor in Domino, id est Deo testante, vel, sub testimonio Domini jubeo, Deum testem adhibendo, ut jam tempore gratiæ, non ambuletis sicut et gentes ambulant, id est, non vivatis sicut gentiles, in vanitate sensus sui, id est diversis erroribus humana vanitate conceptis;
paras.en: Next the Ephesians are instructed in morals, and first they are admonished to turn aside from evil. [[4:17|This then|Hoc igitur]], that is, since so great a grace has been bestowed on you, [[4:17|I say and testify in the Lord|dico et testificor in Domino]], that is, with God as witness; or, I command under the witness of the Lord, calling God to witness, [[4:17|That henceforward|ut jam]], in the time of grace, [[4:17|you walk not as also the Gentiles walk|non ambuletis sicut et gentes ambulant]], that is, that you live not as the heathen, [[4:17|in the vanity of their mind|in vanitate sensus sui]], that is, in divers errors conceived by human vanity;

paras.t: tenebris, id est perfidia variisque falsitatibus, obscuratum habentes intellectum, alienati a via Dei, id est a fide et lege divina, per ignorantiam quæ est in illis (quæ est privatio veritatis, idcirco alienat et separat intellectum a via Dei, quæ pulchra est atque pacifica), propter cæcitatem, id est hebetudinem et duritiam, cordis ipsorum, per quam prædicationi veritatis claudunt oculos mentis. In malevolam enim animam non introibit sapientia.
paras.en: [[4:18|darkened|tenebris]], that is, by faithlessness and various falsehoods, [[4:18|Having their understanding|obscuratum habentes intellectum]], [[4:18|being alienated|alienati]] from the way of God [Denis reads *via*, way, where the Vulgate has *vita*, life], that is, from the faith and the divine law, [[4:18|through the ignorance that is in them|per ignorantiam quæ est in illis]] (which is a privation of truth, and therefore estranges and separates the understanding from the way of God, which is beautiful and peaceable[[Prov 3:17||]]), [[4:18|because of the blindness|propter cæcitatem]], that is, the dullness and hardness, [[4:18|of their hearts|cordis ipsorum]], through which they close the eyes of the mind to the preaching of the truth. For [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul|In malevolam enim animam non introibit sapientia]].

paras.t: Qui desperantes, id est futuræ vitæ ac divinæ remunerationis fiduciam non habentes, semetipsos tradiderunt impudicitiæ, id est turpitudini luxuriæ, procedentes ex concupiscentia in operationem immunditiæ omnis, id est in opera totius fœditatis, nullum genus carnalium voluptatum omittentes, in avaritiam, id est ex peccato luxuriæ etiam in avaritiam lapsi, desiderantes temporalia, sine quorum usu libidini vacare non possunt. De talibus scriptum est per Sapientem: Dixerunt impii apud se: Non est qui agnitus sit reversus ab inferis. Quia ex nihilo nati sumus, et post hæc erimus tanquam non fuerimus. Venite ergo, et fruamur bonis quæ sunt, et utamur creatura tanquam in juventute celeriter; nullum pratum sit quod non pertranseat luxuria nostra.
paras.en: [[4:19|Who despairing|Qui desperantes]], that is, having no confidence in the life to come and in God's reward, [[4:19|have given themselves up to lasciviousness|semetipsos tradiderunt impudicitiæ]], that is, to the foulness of lust, going on from concupiscence [[4:19|unto the working of all uncleanness|in operationem immunditiæ omnis]], that is, to works of every foulness, leaving out no kind of carnal pleasure, [[4:19|unto covetousness|in avaritiam]], that is, fallen from the sin of lust into covetousness as well, desiring temporal things, without the use of which they cannot give themselves to lust. Of such it is written by the Wise man: The wicked [[Wis 2:1|have said|Dixerunt]] within themselves: [[Wis 2:1|no man hath been known to have returned from hell|Non est qui agnitus sit reversus ab inferis]]. [[Wis 2:2|For we are born of nothing, and after this we shall be as if we had not been|Quia ex nihilo nati sumus, et post hæc erimus tanquam non fuerimus]]. [[Wis 2:6|Come, therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that are present, and let us speedily use the creatures as in youth.|Venite ergo, et fruamur bonis quæ sunt, et utamur creatura tanquam in juventute celeriter]] [[Wis 2:8|let no meadow escape our riot|nullum pratum sit quod non pertranseat luxuria nostra]].

paras.t: Vos autem non ita, scilicet ut impudice vivatis, et vitiis gentilitatis vacetis, didicistis Christum, id est Christi doctrinam, quæ docet oppositum; si tamen illum, id est Christi documenta, audistis auribus mentis, id est intellexistis, et in ipso, id est secundum ejus vitam, mores et theoriam, edocti estis a Spiritu Sancto per Christi ministros, sicut est veritas in Jesu: id est, si sic informati estis ut dici possitis edocti in Christo, id est, si vere sapientes estis, vitam et mores conformando scientiæ exemplo Christi, qui cœpit facere et docere.
paras.en: [[4:20|But you have not so|Vos autem non ita]], namely so as to live unchastely and give yourselves to the vices of heathenism, [[4:20|learned Christ|didicistis Christum]], that is, the teaching of Christ, which teaches the opposite; [[4:21|If so be that you have heard him|si tamen illum]], that is, Christ's teachings: heard them with the ears of the mind, that is, understood them; [[4:21|and have been taught in him|et in ipso edocti estis]], that is, according to his life, manners and teaching [*theoriam*, his contemplative doctrine], taught by the Holy Ghost through the ministers of Christ, [[4:21|as the truth is in Jesus|sicut est veritas in Jesu]]: that is, if you have been so formed that you can be said to be taught in Christ; that is, if you are truly wise, conforming your life and manners to your knowledge after the example of Christ, who [[Acts 1:1|began to do and to teach|cœpit facere et docere]].

paras.t: Unde subjungit, quid sit in Christo edoctum esse. Deponere vos secundum pristinam conversationem, id est per abnegationem præcedentium vitiorum, veterem hominem, id est vos ipsos relinquere, quantum ad id quo primo parenti prævaricatori similes estis per inobedientiæ ejus imitationem. Hinc enim dicit Salvator: Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum. Et Salomon loquitur: Verte impios, et non erunt. Qui vetus homo corrumpitur, id est, spiritualiter annihilatur, omne esse gratiæ gratificantis perdendo, secundum desideria erroris, id est consentiendo desideriis pravis, vel ea mancipando effectui. Quæ dicuntur desideria erroris, quia ex errore seu defectu cognitionis aliquo modo procedunt (omnis enim peccans, est ignorans, secundum Philosophum), et ad errorem peccati actualis deducunt. Per veterem autem hominem designatur quilibet nostrum, per comparationem ad pristina vitia, quibus anima vetusta efficitur.
paras.en: Hence he adds what it is to be taught in Christ: [[4:22|To put off, according to former conversation|Deponere vos secundum pristinam conversationem]], that is, by renouncing your former vices, [[4:22|the old man|veterem hominem]], that is, to leave yourselves behind, as to that in which you are like the first parent, the transgressor, by imitating his disobedience. For hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 9:23|If any man will come after me, let him deny himself|Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum]]. And Solomon says: [[Prov 12:7|Turn the wicked, and they shall not be|Verte impios, et non erunt]]. [[4:22|who is corrupted|Qui vetus homo corrumpitur]], that is, is spiritually brought to nothing, losing all the being of sanctifying grace, [[4:22|according to the desire of error|secundum desideria erroris]], that is, by consenting to wicked desires, or by carrying them into effect. And these are called desires of error because in some way they proceed from error or a defect of knowledge (for everyone who sins is ignorant, according to the Philosopher), and they lead to the error of actual sin. By the old man, then, is meant any one of us, in relation to the former vices by which the soul is made old.

paras.t: Deinde Apostolus exhortatur Ephesios ad operationem boni. Renovamini autem spiritu, id est affectu, mentis, id est animæ, vestræ; vel, Spiritu mentis vestræ, id est spiritu qui est mens vestra. Quid autem sit taliter renovari, additur:
paras.en: Then the Apostle exhorts the Ephesians to do good. [[4:23|And be renewed in spirit|Renovamini autem spiritu]], that is, in affection, [[4:23|of your mind|mentis]], that is, of your soul; or, In spirit of your mind, that is, in the spirit which is your mind. And what it is to be so renewed is added:

paras.t: et induite novum hominem, id est, similitudinem Christi, vel cujuscumque hominis spiritualis in Christo renati ac renovati, assumite, ejus sequendo vestigia (sicut superius dictum est: Induimini Dominum Jesum): hoc est, esse virtutum et gratiæ adipisci curate, ut quotidie in caritate et gratia proficientes, indesinenter recentes et vigorosi, imo in dies magis recentiores fiatis. Qui novus homo secundum Deum, id est a Deo seu operatione divina, vel secundum beneplacitum Dei, creatus, id est formatus vel reformatus, est in justitia et sanctitate veritatis, id est puritate vera, non simulata. Has enim virtutes Christus, secundum quod homo, accepit quando in utero Virginis creata est anima ejus, et corpori suo unita. Alii vero in Baptismo et Pœnitentia eas recipiunt.
paras.en: [[4:24|And put on the new man|et induite novum hominem]], that is, take on the likeness of Christ, or of any spiritual man reborn and renewed in Christ, by following in his footsteps (as was said above: [[Rom 13:14|put ye on the Lord Jesus|Induimini Dominum Jesum]]); that is, be careful to gain the being of the virtues and of grace, so that, advancing daily in charity and grace, you may be ceaselessly fresh and vigorous, nay, become fresher from day to day. [[4:24|who according to God|Qui novus homo secundum Deum]], that is, by God or the divine working, or according to God's good pleasure, [[4:24|is created|creatus]], that is, formed or re-formed, [[4:24|in justice and holiness of truth|est in justitia et sanctitate veritatis]], that is, in true purity, not feigned. For Christ, as man, received these virtues when his soul was created in the Virgin's womb and united to his body; but others receive them in Baptism and Penance.

paras.t: Propter quod deponentes mendacium, quod veritati et per consequens Deo, qui veritas est, adversatur: deponentes, inquam, omne mendacium, scilicet officiosum, jocosum, et maxime perniciosum, de quo in libro Sapientiæ habetur: Os quod mentitur, occidit animam; et in Psalmo, Perdes omnes qui loquuntur mendacium; loquimini veritatem, id est verum sermonem, unusquisque cum proximo suo, id est quolibet homine, qui secundum naturam tibi frater et proximus est: nam et Pater unus omnium nostrum, et Deus unus creavit nos; quoniam sumus invicem membra, id est per modum membrorum uniti, ad idem corpus Ecclesiæ pertinentes, atque ad mutuam subventionem obligati. Hinc per Prophetam dicitur: Veritatem tantum et pacem diligite.
paras.en: [[4:25|Wherefore, putting away lying|Propter quod deponentes mendacium]], which is opposed to truth, and consequently to God, who is truth: putting away, I say, every lie, namely the officious [that is, told to help someone or avert harm], the jocose [told in jest], and above all the pernicious [told to do harm], of which it is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 1:11|the mouth that belieth, killeth the soul|Os quod mentitur, occidit animam]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 5:7|thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie|Perdes omnes qui loquuntur mendacium]]; [[4:25|speak ye the truth|loquimini veritatem]], that is, true speech, [[4:25|every man with his neighbour|unusquisque cum proximo suo]], that is, with any man, who by nature is thy brother and neighbour: for we have all [[Mal 2:10|one father|Pater unus omnium nostrum]], and [[Mal 2:10|one God created us|Deus unus creavit nos]]; [[4:25|For we are members one of another|quoniam sumus invicem membra]], that is, united after the manner of members, belonging to the same body of the Church[[Rom 12:5||]][[1 Cor 12:12||]], and bound to help one another.
