[[6:11|that you may be able to stand|Ut possitis stare]], that is, to fight bravely and prevail, [[6:11|against the deceits|adversus insidias]], that is, the hidden machinations, [[6:11|of the devil|diaboli]], who often [[2 Cor 11:14|transformeth himself into an angel of light|transfigurat in angelum lucis]], putting forward many evils under the appearance of good. In short, as Pope Leo testifies, he examines the ways of all, sifts their cares, searches out their affections; and there he seeks occasions of harming, where he sees anyone most eagerly occupied.

paras.t: Quoniam non est nobis colluctatio principalis aut sola adversus carnem et sanguinem, id est homines carnales et fragiles, seu vitia carnis. Unde Dominus in Genesi ait : Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est; et in Evangelio, Caro et sanguis non revelavit tibi. Verumtamen grave bellum habemus contra carnem et sanguinem, id est mundum et concupiscentiæ carnis. Bellum vero quod contra hostes invisibiles habemus, periculosissimum est atque gravissimum. De quibus subjungitur : sed adversus principes et potestates, id est angelos apostatas seu dæmones, qui erant ante lapsum suum de ordinibus Principatuum et Potestatum. De omnibus enim angelorum ordinibus quidam cecidisse creduntur, qui omnes jam per principatus et potestates designantur : ita quod nomine principatuum designantur dæmones inferiores ; nomine autem potestatum, superiores, quibus inferiores obediunt, homines impugnando. Est enim in dæmonibus prælatio quædam, eo quod omnes concordes sint in desiderio nocendi hominibus. Adversus mundi rectores, id est contra prædictos invisibiles hostes, hominum sæcularium directores ac principes. Homines enim iniqui dæmonum voluntati obediunt, et ab ipsis captivi tenentur, ac undique circumferuntur sicut servi a dominis. Et ne quis per mundum putaret significari machinam mundialem, quasi diabolus creator et rector esset mundi sensibilis, sicut Manichæi dixerunt, ob id se ipsum exponens Apostolus, subdidit : tenebrarum harum, id est hominum obtenebratorum. Unde paulo ante inductum est : Fuistis aliquando tenebræ. Hoc modo mundus frequenter accipitur in Scripturis : sicut quum dicitur, Mundus eum non cognovit ; et, Mundus in maligno positus est ; et, Non estis de mundo. Contra spiritualia nequitiæ, id est agmina dæmonum nequitiis plena, habitantia in cœlestibus, id est in aere caliginoso, in quo dæmones complures usque ad diem judicii volitant. Aer autem sæpius cœlum vocatur. Hinc namque dicuntur volucres cœli, qui asseruntur volare in cœlo, id est in aere. Unde et dæmones significantur per volucres cœli, ubi ait Salvator : Semen cecidit secus viam, et volucres cœli comederunt illud.
paras.en: [[6:12|For our wrestling is not|Quoniam non est nobis colluctatio]] chiefly or solely [[6:12|against flesh and blood|adversus carnem et sanguinem]], that is, carnal and frail men, or the vices of the flesh. Hence the Lord says in Genesis: [[Gen 6:3|My spirit shall not remain in man for ever, because he is flesh|Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est]]; and in the Gospel, [[Matt 16:17|flesh and blood hath not revealed it to thee|Caro et sanguis non revelavit tibi]]. Yet we have a heavy war against flesh and blood, that is, the world and the concupiscences of the flesh. But the war we have against invisible enemies is the most perilous and the heaviest. Of these is added: [[6:12|but against principalities and powers|sed adversus principes et potestates]], that is, the apostate angels or demons, who before their fall were of the orders of the Principalities and Powers. For some of every order of angels are believed to have fallen, and all of them are now designated by principalities and powers: so that by the name of principalities the lower demons are designated, and by the name of powers the higher, whom the lower obey in assailing men. For there is among the demons a certain rule of superiors, because all are of one mind in the desire of harming men. [[6:12|against the rulers of the world|Adversus mundi rectores]], that is, against the aforesaid invisible enemies, the directors and princes of worldly men. For wicked men obey the will of the demons, and are held captive by them, and are carried about everywhere like slaves by their masters. And lest anyone should think that by *world* is meant the fabric of the world [Latin *machina mundialis*, the visible universe], as though the devil were the creator and ruler of the sensible world, as the Manichees said, the Apostle, explaining himself, added: [[6:12|of this darkness|tenebrarum harum]], that is, of darkened men. Hence it was said a little before: [[Eph 5:8|you were heretofore darkness|Fuistis aliquando tenebræ]]. In this way *world* is often taken in the Scriptures: as when it is said, [[John 1:10|the world knew him not|Mundus eum non cognovit]]; and, The [[1 John 5:19|world is seated in wickedness|Mundus in maligno positus est]]; and, [[John 15:19|you are not of the world|Non estis de mundo]] [no margin reference here; the words are those of John 15:19]. [[6:12|against the spirits of wickedness|Contra spiritualia nequitiæ]], that is, the hosts of demons full of wickedness, dwelling [[6:12|in the high places|in cœlestibus]], that is, in the dark air, in which many demons fly about until the day of judgment. For the air is quite often called heaven. Hence birds are called *birds of heaven* [Latin *volucres cœli*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "fowls of the air"], being said to fly in heaven, that is, in the air. And so demons too are signified by the birds of heaven, where the Saviour says: The seed: [[Luke 8:5|some fell by the way side|cecidit secus viam]], and [[Luke 8:5|the fowls of the air devoured it|volucres cœli comederunt illud]] [the margin gives Luc. xiii, 5; the words are Luke 8:5].

paras.t: Propterea, id est, quia tam arduum prælium imminet vobis, accipite armaturam Dei, id est virtutes et opera virtuosa, quibus dæmones repelluntur : de quibus armis Job ait, Justitia indutus sum, et vestivi me ea sicut vestimento, et diademate judicio meo ; ut possitis resistere diabolo, qui tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret, in die malo, id est tempore tentationis et adversitatis, et in omnibus prosperis et adversis perfecti stare, ruinam vitando peccati, ita ut nec prospera vos extollant, neque adversa dejiciant, sed regia semper via incedatis, utentes utraque manu pro dextera, quatenus omnia cooperentur vobis in bonum.
paras.en: [[6:13|Therefore|Propterea]], that is, because so hard a battle threatens you, [[6:13|take unto you the armour of God|accipite armaturam Dei]], that is, virtues and virtuous works, by which demons are driven back: of which arms Job says, [[Job 29:14|I was clad with justice: and I clothed myself with my judgment, as with a robe and a diadem|Justitia indutus sum, et vestivi me ea sicut vestimento, et diademate judicio meo]] [the margin gives Job xxx, 14; the words are Job 29:14]; [[6:13|that you may be able to resist|ut possitis resistere]] the devil, who [[1 Pet 5:8|as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret]], [[6:13|in the evil day|in die malo]], that is, in the time of temptation and adversity, [[6:13|and to stand in all things|et in omnibus]], prosperous and adverse, [[6:13|perfect|perfecti stare]], avoiding the ruin of sin, so that prosperity does not lift you up nor adversity cast you down, but you walk always by the royal road, using either hand as the right[[Judg 3:15||]] [the margin gives Judic. iii, 1; the phrase is said of Aod at Judg 3:15; that is, turning prosperity and adversity alike to good], so that [[Rom 8:28|all things work together unto good|omnia cooperentur vobis in bonum]] for you.

paras.t: State ergo in virtutibus fixi, succincti cingulo castitatis lumbos vestros, in quibus viget luxuria, id est, carnis concupiscentias refrenate, continenter vivendo, prout monet Salvator : Sint lumbi vestri præcincti. Hos lumbos præcinxit Job : Pepigi, inquiens, fœdus cum oculis meis, ut ne cogitarem quidem de virgine. Sic autem accingite lumbos in veritate, id est, veraciter coram Deo, non simulatorie coram hominibus, sicut hypocritæ. Et induti loricam justitiæ, id est, virtute justitiæ interiora vestra munite, sicut lorica corpus tegitur ac munitur. Unde apud Isaiam dicitur : Indumento justitiæ circumdedit me Dominus.
paras.en: [[6:14|Stand therefore|State ergo]], fixed in virtues, [[6:14|girt about|succincti]] with the girdle of chastity as to [[6:14|your loins|lumbos vestros]], in which lust thrives; that is, rein in the concupiscences of the flesh by living continently, as the Saviour warns: [[Luke 12:35|Let your loins be girt|Sint lumbi vestri præcincti]]. These loins Job girded: [[Job 31:1|I made|Pepigi]], he says, [[Job 31:1|a covenant with my eyes, that I would not so much as think upon a virgin|fœdus cum oculis meis, ut ne cogitarem quidem de virgine]]. And thus gird your loins [[6:14|with truth|in veritate]], that is, truly before God, not feignedly before men, as hypocrites do. [[6:14|And having on the breastplate of justice|Et induti loricam justitiæ]], that is, fortify your inner parts with the virtue of justice, as the body is covered and fortified by a breastplate. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 61:10|with the robe of justice he hath covered me|Indumento justitiæ circumdedit me]], namely the Lord.

paras.t: Et calceati pedes, id est, pedes corporales, et etiam spirituales, id est animi vestri affectiones, habete munitos et expeditos, in præparatione Evangelii pacis, id est ad hoc ut sitis parati annuntiare vel adimplere evangelicam doctrinam, in qua pacificatio nostra cum Deo describitur, et per cujus observantiam veram pacem sortimur, juxta illud in Psalmo : Pax multa diligentibus legem tuam.
paras.en: [[6:15|And your feet shod|Et calceati pedes]], that is, have your feet, the bodily ones and the spiritual ones too, that is, the affections of your soul, protected and ready, [[6:15|with the preparation of the gospel of peace|in præparatione Evangelii pacis]], that is, so that you may be prepared to announce or to fulfil the gospel teaching, in which our being set at peace with God is described, and by the keeping of which we obtain true peace, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 118:165|Much peace have they that love thy law|Pax multa diligentibus legem tuam]].

paras.t: In omnibus spiritualibus pugnis seu tentamentis sumentes scutum fidei, id est, ipsam fidem pro scuto arripite, virtutem et actum fidei opponentes suggestionibus dæmonis, puta futura tormenta inferni, sempiterna gaudia cœli, metuendum judicium Dei, quæ omnia cadunt sub fide : per quorum utique considerationem omnia tentamenta vincuntur. Ideo subditur : in quo scuto possitis omnia tela nequissimi ignea, id est impugnationes acres ac fervidas pessimi tentatoris, exstinguere, id est reprimere. Propter quod Petrus ait : Adversarius vester diabolus circuit, quærens quem devoret ; cui resistite fortes in fide.
paras.en: [[6:16|In all things|In omnibus]], that is, in all spiritual fights or temptations, [[6:16|taking the shield of faith|sumentes scutum fidei]], that is, take up faith itself for a shield, setting the virtue and act of faith against the suggestions of the demon: for instance, the future torments of hell, the everlasting joys of heaven, the dreadful judgment of God, all of which fall under faith; and by considering these all temptations are overcome. Therefore it is added: [[6:16|wherewith you may be able|in quo scuto possitis]] [Latin *in quo scuto*, in which shield] [[6:16|to extinguish|exstinguere]], that is, to repress, [[6:16|all the fiery darts of the most wicked one|omnia tela nequissimi ignea]], that is, the sharp and burning assaults of the worst of tempters. Wherefore Peter says: [[1 Pet 5:8|your adversary the devil|Adversarius vester diabolus]] [[1 Pet 5:8|goeth about seeking whom he may devour|circuit, quærens quem devoret]]; [[1 Pet 5:9|Whom resist ye, strong in faith|cui resistite fortes in fide]].

paras.t: Et galeam salutis assumite, id est, spem futuræ felicitatis seu caritatem menti vestræ superponite, ut contra præsentium bonorum blandimenta, spe futurorum atque divino amore armemini, et gladium spiritus, id est a Spiritu Sancto datum spiritui vestro, quod est verbum Dei, id est sermo sacræ Scripturæ, qui penetrat intima animæ, et vitia resecat, atque a mundo animam dividit, sicut materialis gladius penetrat corpus. De hoc gladio spirituali dicit Salvator : Non veni pacem mittere, sed gladium ; et Psalmista, Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum, potentissime.
paras.en: [[6:17|And take unto you the helmet of salvation|Et galeam salutis assumite]], that is, set the hope of future happiness, or charity, upon your mind, so that against the allurements of present goods you may be armed with the hope of things to come and with divine love, [[6:17|and the sword of the Spirit|et gladium spiritus]] [Latin *spiritus*, which Denis takes both of the Holy Ghost and of your own spirit], that is, given by the Holy Ghost to your spirit, [[6:17|which is the word of God|quod est verbum Dei]], that is, the speech of sacred Scripture, which pierces the inmost parts of the soul, and cuts away vices, and divides the soul from the world[[Heb 4:12||]], as a material sword pierces the body. Of this spiritual sword the Saviour says: [[Matt 10:34|I came not to send peace, but the sword|Non veni pacem mittere, sed gladium]]; and the Psalmist, [[Ps 44:4|Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O thou most mighty|Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum, potentissime]].

paras.t: Sed quia hæc omnia ex divino auxilio manant, atque per gratiam conferuntur devote orantibus, ideo subditur : Per omnem orationem, id est prædicta implete, Deum invocando per omnem, id est perfectam, orationem. Est autem oratio simplex petitio ; obsecratio vero, est petitio cum adjuratione seu commemoratione rei sacræ, sicut quum dicimus : Per incarnationem tuam libera nos, Domine. De qua nunc sequitur : et obsecrationem, quæ etiam proprie est respectu difficilium, orantes omni tempore, id est singulis horis deputatis et debitis vel congruis ad orandum, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico habetur : Non impediaris orare semper. Unde et Salvator : Oportet, inquit, semper orare et non deficere. In spiritu, id est cum devotionis affectu, seu attentione mentali. Spiritus enim est Deus, et eos qui adorant eum, in spiritu et veritate oportet adorare. Et in ipso vigilantes, id est solliciti atque ferventes, in omni instantia, id est conamine quo actibus virtuosis insistitur, et obsecratione fusa pro omnibus sanctis viatoribus, ut perseverent proficiantque in bonis ;
paras.en: But since all these things flow from divine help, and are conferred through grace on those who pray devoutly, it is therefore added: [[6:18|By all prayer|Per omnem orationem]], that is, fulfil the things aforesaid by calling upon God with all, that is, with perfect, prayer. Now prayer [Latin *oratio*] is simple petition; but supplication [*obsecratio*] is petition with an adjuration or a commemoration of some sacred thing, as when we say: By thy incarnation deliver us, O Lord [from the Litany of the Saints]. Of this there now follows: [[6:18|and supplication|et obsecrationem]], which also properly concerns difficult things, [[6:18|praying at all times|orantes omni tempore]], that is, at the several hours appointed and due or fitting for prayer, as we have in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 18:22|Let nothing hinder thee from praying always|Non impediaris orare semper]]. Hence the Saviour too: [[Luke 18:1|we ought|Oportet]], He says, [[Luke 18:1|always to pray and not to faint|semper orare et non deficere]]. [[6:18|in the spirit|In spiritu]], that is, with the affection of devotion, or with attention of the mind. For [[John 4:24|God is a spirit: and they that adore him must adore him in spirit and in truth|Spiritus enim est Deus, et eos qui adorant eum, in spiritu et veritate oportet adorare]]. [[6:18|and in the same watching|Et in ipso vigilantes]], that is, solicitous and fervent, [[6:18|with all instance|in omni instantia]], that is, with the effort by which one presses on in virtuous acts, [[6:18|and supplication|et obsecratione]] poured out [[6:18|for all the saints|pro omnibus sanctis]] still on the way [Latin *viatoribus*, wayfarers: those still in this life], that they may persevere and make progress in good things.

paras.t: et pro me, ut detur mihi sermo in apertione oris mei, id est, quatenus Spiritus Sanctus mentem illuminet, ita ut mox dum os meum ad loquendum aperio, infundatur mihi a Deo quid loqui expediat : sicut et Deus promisit in Psalmo, Dilata os tuum, et implebo illud ; et item in Evangelio, Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam ; cum fiducia, id est secure et libere, notum facere mysterium Evangelii, id est sacrum secretum evangelicæ legis, videlicet Christi incarnationem et cetera ejus mysteria. Ponitur enim singulare pro plurali.
paras.en: [[6:19|And for me, that speech may be given me|et pro me, ut detur mihi sermo]], [[6:19|that I may open my mouth|in apertione oris mei]], that is, that the Holy Ghost may enlighten my mind, so that as soon as I open my mouth to speak, what it is expedient to say may be poured into me by God: as God also promised in the Psalm, [[Ps 80:11|open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it|Dilata os tuum, et implebo illud]]; and likewise in the Gospel, [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam]]; [[6:19|with confidence|cum fiducia]], that is, securely and freely, [[6:19|to make known the mystery of the gospel|notum facere mysterium Evangelii]], that is, the sacred secret of the gospel law, namely Christ's incarnation and His other mysteries. For the singular is put for the plural.

paras.t: Pro quo Evangelio prædicando legatione fungor, id est, a Christo destinatus sum, nunc Romæ exsistens in catena, id est in vinculis ; ita legatione fungor et vinculis stringor, ut nihilo minus in ipso, id est per gratiam Christi, audeam fiducialiter, prout oportet me, id est, sicut commissum est mihi, loqui, evangelica mysteria prædicando.
paras.en: [[6:20|For which|Pro quo]] gospel, for preaching it, [[6:20|I am an ambassador|legatione fungor]], that is, I have been sent by Christ, being now at Rome [[6:20|in a chain|in catena]], that is, in bonds[[Acts 28:20||]]; thus am I an ambassador and bound with chains, so that none the less [[6:20|therein|in ipso]], that is, through the grace of Christ, [[6:20|I may be bold|audeam]] confidently, [[6:20|according as I ought|prout oportet me]], that is, as has been committed to me, [[6:20|to speak|loqui]], by preaching the mysteries of the gospel.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Apostolus dilectionem suam ad Ephesios, insinuando eis statum suum, quemadmodum pertinet ad familiares amicos. Ut autem et vos sciatis quæ circa me sunt, id est quæ mihi contingunt, quid agam in tot persecutionibus ; omnia hæc nota vobis faciet, id est, ore tenus reserabit, Tychicus diaconus, lator præsentis epistolæ, carissimus frater noster spiritualis, et fidelis minister in Domino, id est secundum voluntatem et gratiam Dei ; vel, In Domino, id est in his quæ Dei sunt ; quem misi ad vos in hoc ipsum, id est propter hanc causam, ut cognoscatis ex ejus veridica relatione, quæ circa nos sunt, id est prospera et adversa quæ accidunt nobis, et consoletur corda vestra de mei captione et catenatione dolentia.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows his love for the Ephesians by making his state known to them, as is fitting among familiar friends. [[6:21|But that you also may know|Ut autem et vos sciatis]] [[6:21|the things that concern me|quæ circa me sunt]], that is, what befalls me, [[6:21|and what I am doing|quid agam]] amid so many persecutions, [[6:21|Tychicus|Tychicus]] the deacon, the bearer of the present epistle, our [[6:21|dearest brother|carissimus frater]] in the spirit, [[6:21|and faithful minister in the Lord|et fidelis minister in Domino]], that is, according to the will and grace of God, or, [[6:21|in the Lord|In Domino]], that is, in the things that are God's, [[6:21|will make known to you all things|omnia hæc nota vobis faciet]], that is, will disclose them by word of mouth; [[6:22|Whom I have sent to you for this same purpose|quem misi ad vos in hoc ipsum]], that is, for this cause, [[6:22|that you may know|ut cognoscatis]] from his truthful report [[6:22|the things concerning us|quæ circa nos sunt]], that is, the prosperous and adverse things that happen to us, [[6:22|and that he may comfort your hearts|et consoletur corda vestra]], grieving over my capture and my chains.

paras.t: Porro ut finis epistolæ concordet principio, addit : Pax sit fratribus, id est fidelibus : quo nomine sorores quoque intelliguntur ; et caritas cum fide, id est caritas et fides, detur vobis a Deo Patre nostro, id est a Patre æterno, et Domino Jesu Christo Filio Patris : quibus expressis, intelligitur Spiritus Sanctus.
paras.en: Further, so that the end of the epistle may agree with its beginning, he adds: [[6:23|Peace be to the brethren|Pax sit fratribus]], that is, to the faithful: under which name the sisters too are understood; [[6:23|and charity with faith|et caritas cum fide]], that is, charity and faith, be given you [[6:23|from God the Father|a Deo Patre]], our Father, that is, from the eternal Father, [[6:23|and the Lord Jesus Christ|et Domino Jesu Christo]], the Son of the Father: and with these named, the Holy Ghost is understood.

paras.t: Gratia Dei gratificans et finalis, sit cum omnibus qui diligunt Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum. Quod vero subjungitur, in incorruptione, referri potest ad nomen, Gratia, eritque sensus, Gratia sit cum eis in incorruptione, id est in vita æterna ; vel ad verbum, Diligunt, ut sit sensus. Qui diligunt Christum in incorruptione, id est in cordis ac fidei integritate, seu inconcussa mentis constantia. Sic enim amandus est Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[6:24|Grace|Gratia]] of God, grace that makes pleasing, and final grace [that is, sanctifying grace, which makes one pleasing to God, and the grace of final perseverance], be [[6:24|with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ|cum omnibus qui diligunt Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum]]. As for what is added, [[6:24|in incorruption|in incorruptione]], it may be referred to the noun *Grace*, and the sense will be: Grace be with them in incorruption, that is, in eternal life; or to the verb *love*, so that the sense is: Who love Christ in incorruption, that is, in integrity of heart and of faith, or in unshaken constancy of mind. For so is God, sublime and blessed, to be loved. [[6:24|Amen|Amen]].
